question.problem:
Find $\text{E}[X{Y}^{3}],$ given that random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{9{y}^{2}},\, & 0\le x\le {y}^{3},\,0\le y\le 3; \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are continuous random variables, and $f(x,y)$ is their joint probability density function. If $r:{R}^{2}\to R$ is a function of two variables, then the rule of the lazy statistician states that

$$
\text{E}[r(X,Y)]={∬}_{{R}^{2}}r(x,y)\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
r(x,y)=x{y}^{3}.
$$

Now, let's sketch the region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le {y}^{3},\,0\le y\le 3\},$ where $f(x,y)$ is nonzero.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14161553/assets/68da52d856f882614241d72cff4dc3f5947cf16a6c9f58b0aea1c58d7eb375cc.png)

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X{Y}^{3}] & ={∬}_{{R}^{2}}x{y}^{3}\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={∬}_{D}x{y}^{3}\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{3}}x{y}^{3}\cdot \frac{2}{9{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{9}{\int }_{0}^{3}y{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{3}}x\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{9}{\int }_{0}^{3}y{[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x={y}^{3}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{9}{\int }_{0}^{3}{y}^{7}\text{ }\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{9}{[\frac{{y}^{8}}{8}]}_{y=0}^{y=3} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}(\frac{{3}^{8}}{8}) \\  & =\frac{729}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
